Dear Central Disclosure Team,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where it applies, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004.

It concerns the demolition of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan (national grid reference ST 1670 7335). Contemporary press reports record that the farmhouse was demolished in early December 1988. The site is recorded in the Heneb Historic Environment Record as GGAT02038s.

Please could you tell me whether HSE or HM Factory Inspectorate holds any of the following for the period 1 October 1988 to 30 June 1989:

1. any notification received about demolition or building operations at this site under the legislation then in force, including the name of the contractor and of the person or company for whom the work was done;
2. any record of an inspector's visit, inspection, enforcement action or reported incident at the site in that period;
3. any index or register entry showing that such a notification or visit was recorded, even if the file itself no longer exists.

If no information is held, please tell me:
(a) which record series and systems were searched, including any historic paper indexes;
(b) the retention period that applied to such notifications and inspection records in 1988–89; and
(c) whether any transfer or disposal record exists for them.

I would be grateful for the information by email. A short acknowledgement with your reference number would be very helpful.

Kind regards,

Requester

texts.gm-1a19b45e6cd2d5ae:
Dear Historic Buildings & Places,

I am researching the history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan (approx. ST 168 733), the house beside St Dochdwy's Church. The family's recorded transcription of the index to an 1824 Bute estate survey (Glamorgan Archives, DB/E/1, plan 19) gives the name "Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm". The house was demolished in late 1988. The South Wales Echo of 3 December 1988 ("History fight to save farm") reported that Cadw was considering spot-listing the farmhouse and that an inspector was due to visit that weekend.

As the Ancient Monuments Society was a national amenity society for England and Wales at that time, please could you tell me whether the Society's casework records include anything about the house, for example:

1. any notification, request for spot-listing, or correspondence about its threatened demolition in 1988–89; or
2. any earlier record of the building.

If such records exist, I would be grateful for a reference and a short description, and to know whether they are held by the Society or have been deposited with an archive.

I would welcome a short acknowledgement.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear HER Team,

Thank you for your three replies of 2 November 2026: on "Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff", on my request about the Llandough Roman villa and medieval house finds and the 1983 fire, and on my nomenclature supplement.

I would be grateful if Heneb would reconsider those answers, for these reasons.

1. Search, not research. I am not asking Heneb to research or interpret anything. I am asking whether the Historic Environment Record you maintain holds entries, files or correspondence under the names, grid references and dates I listed, and what searches were made to establish that. Searching your own record for named entries is part of answering a request, not research on my behalf.

2. The regime. The HER is kept on behalf of the Welsh Ministers under sections 194 and 195 of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023. Information about cultural sites and built structures is environmental information under regulation 2(1)(f) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, and information held by another body on behalf of a public authority is held by that authority (regulation 3(2)(b)). I therefore ask that my requests be reconsidered as they would be under regulation 11 of the Regulations. If Heneb's view is that the Regulations do not apply to the HER, please tell me so and on what basis, so that I can put the same requests to the Welsh Ministers.

3. The searches made. For the 1983 fire and Roman villa request, please confirm whether the search covered the paper HER files and the GGAT archive for 1983 to 1989 and the names in my supplement, or the online Archwilio database only.

I would be grateful for your answer within 40 working days, as regulation 11(4) provides.


Kind regards,

Requester
